summary: A review that finishes normally leaves its 300 s wall-clock watchdog armed because only join() disarms it, so the timer later reports a false wall_timeout and runs native cancel on the finished review.
failure_scenario: A review is admitted and finishes with outcome 'finished', and no later review request or close for that conversation calls join() within 300 s. _finished() records the outcome but neither cancels running.watchdog nor removes _active[conversation_id]. At 300 s _expire() sees the same review_id still active, prints [voice-review] {"refusal":"wall_timeout"} and calls cancel_and_join(). That sets running.cancelled and calls port.cancel(parent, token) with the token that finish() already released. The review outcome stays 'finished', so no data is lost. The false refusal evidence and the stray native cancel call are the consequences.
evidence: Static read of review.py:326-331, 374-385, 459-463, 484-488. Synthetic run with the tests' FakeReviewPort and FakeHermes, with pytest and aiohttp stubbed because they are not installed, and _REVIEW_WALL_SECONDS=0.3. Control: review finishes, join() is called, wait 0.6 s -> cancel_calls=0, no marker. Defect: review finishes, no join, wait 0.6 s -> marker wall_timeout printed, cancel_calls=1, outcome still 'finished'. test_stale_watchdog_cannot_cancel_successor_review covers only the successor-review case, not this one. The same stale-watchdog path does not reach a successor review, because the next review request calls join() first, which cancels the timer.

summary: _newest_outcome compares generations across tail resets, so after the tail resets to generation 0 a stale higher-generation delete outcome is kept and a delete that genuinely completed is never reported complete.
failure_scenario: The delete record holds outcome ('prev', 5) and the tail file is absent, unreadable or has no archive identity. open() runs _fresh() or the 'unproven' retire path, so the binding restarts at generation 0 while the record keeps outcome gen 5. The user forgets the new gen-0 conversation. request_forget() and acknowledge_forget() both call _newest_outcome(), which keeps ('prev', 5) because 5 > 0, so the outcome never becomes the binding just deleted. host_launcher.py:2822 (`writer.delete_outcome == old_binding`) returns 'pending' even after the companion verified completion, and deleted_previous (outcome gen + 1 == generation) stays False, so voice_delete_status() is 'idle' instead of 'complete'. The delete itself is done in Hermes; only the completion claim is lost, and later deletes are blocked from reporting complete.
evidence: Static read of voice_tail.py:908, 948-952, 994-1010, 1311-1352, 1405-1425 and host_launcher.py:2822, 2862. Synthetic run with a real VoiceTailWriter and ConversationContextStore in a temp dir. Control: no deletes record -> after request_forget, outcome=('c0',0), deleted_previous=True. Defect: deletes record with outcome ('prev',5) and live ('lv',6), no tail file -> after request_forget, pending=(), outcome=('prev',5), binding=('c1',1), deleted_previous=False. The module docstring names a corrupt or reset tail as a designed case, and no test covers a reset to generation 0 with a higher recorded outcome.

summary: Prior claim review.py:276 (a replayed request whose earlier run ended 'cancelled' is acknowledged 'accepted' and not re-run): accepted tradeoff, not a distinct defect. The ledger entry was already acknowledged on first admission, and the sender advances coverage on that ack. A cancel after admission loses the window with or without a replay. A reserved or unknown outcome is correctly refused 'unknown' and a failed one 'failed', so no duplicate spawn or false started claim arises. The distinct bug is the false cancel in the finding above.
Prior claim voice_tail.py:1008: reproduced (see finding). It needs a tail reset while the delete record survives, so it is an edge case rather than steady-state.

companion/forget.py reconciler, voice_forget.py sender and store.tombstone: read in full. Tombstone is persisted before any native delete. Targets and copies are frozen before deletion, and a replay reuses the same manifest. Completion needs a verified absence, and on_complete runs before mark_delete_complete, so a failure there stays pending. A refused or unbound binding stays pending and is retried with backoff, which is fail-closed and not a lost terminal. The sender settles only on an exact binding match plus acknowledge_forget. No defect found.

voice_memory.py receiver (binding re-check per event, revision monotonic, memory cleared in finally, retaining refusals only for the listed categories), memory.py snapshot bounds, and voice_deletes.py record parse/serialise round trip: read, no defect found. I did not exercise them dynamically.

Not verified or out of scope: assigned-file bodies of archive.py, integrity.py, hermes_compat.py, attestation.py, host.py and most of store.py and voice_tail.py/voice_archive.py were not exhaustively audited, so absence of findings there is not a soundness claim. Prior claims in files outside this slice (api.py, plugin.py, bridge.py, scripts/*, web/*, sqlite_spool.py, worker.py, knowledge.py and others) were not assessed. pytest, aiohttp and uv dependencies are not installed, so the full suite, ruff and mypy were not run. The two reproductions used stub modules and the tests' own fakes.
